
## GitHub repository

The group assignment was developed in Python using Visual Studio Code (VS Code) and managed through a public GitHub repository:

https://github.com/jenniferhoumard/IEAP-Python-Series03-Group

To organize the group work, one member initially created the GitHub repository, added the other members as collaborators, and prepared the master Quarto document and separate subsection files (.qmd). The headings and subsections were predefined according to the assignment requirements so that each member had a clear structure to follow and knew exactly where to add their work. This also allowed members to work on their assigned files independently, reducing overlap and potential conflicts.

The assignment was developed in Python using Visual Studio Code (VS Code). Quarto (.qmd) files were used to combine Python code, explanations, tables, and plots in the same document. The master Quarto file brings together all the subsections into a single report with consistent headings, automatic numbering, and a table of contents.

## Branching strategy

We adopted a feature-branch workflow, creating one branch for each of the five main sections of the assignment:

1. Group workflow and division of tasks between group members

2. Create functions to find and plot remarkable points

3. Analyze a known signal

4. Redo the analysis with a noisy signal

5. Critical points and problem solving

Each branch is dedicated to its corresponding section, allowing group members to work independently without modifying the same files.

All branches originate from the main branch. Once a section is completed, the responsible student commits and pushes their changes to GitHub, then creates a pull request for review before merging into main.

As the technical sections are dependent on one another, Sections 2, 3, and 4 are integrated in sequence to ensure that the functions and variables required by later sections are available. The documentation sections can be developed separately.

This approach keeps the main branch as the integrated version of the assignment while maintaining a clear commit history and individual contributions.
